column1: # North Britanny's inn (dialog byte 0x88) at 13:00 (cleak/u5-spec#238).
# Seeded rather than walked to. The walk-up form of this scenario scripted its
# way in from the town gate, and the resident walks its own schedule while
# those steps run, so the two sides arrived with it in different cells and
# every later beat compared unrelated windows (`cleak/u5-engine#22`).
# `qa/tools/reseed.py` replayed that walk once into the seed named below.
# `shops.md` §2: a shopkeeper's "conversation-contact event also reaches it
# automatically during a town schedule pass, even if the player has issued no
# Talk command", so the first Pass beside the keeper opens the overlay and the
# script drives it from there rather than issuing Talk.
# requires-seed: profile `seed-nb-inn-reseeded`, built by qa/tools/reseed.py
# The entry greeting is a lottery. `shops.md` Section 8.A draws the innkeeper's
# opening bark from a four-record pool, and `prng.md` Section 3 seeds the two
# sides from the host clock at the intro menu, so they never draw the same row.
# Measured 2026-09-11: the original opened with `...adventurer. My name is
# Terbor, and I own this hostel. May I help thee?"` and this engine with
# `Terbor, the innkeeper. Is there anything I can do for thee?" `. Every beat
# from the greeting onward therefore compares unlike text in the rows above the
# service question; the question itself and everything below it agree exactly.
# A difference confined to those greeting rows must be re-run before it means
# anything.
# The `talk` beat reads `record-wide` rather than a legal pool draw on most
# runs, because the greeting's length also decides the entry prompt's
# punctuation (`shops.md` Section 8.B: the colon is conditional on the
# finished greeting's column), so a different draw changes the row under it
# as well. From 2026-10-13 to the rc7 sweep this scenario read 2 matches and
# 14 such re-runs; rc6's match (20261022-143317) was a lucky pair of draws,
# not a baseline, and rc7's two runs (20261022-225655, 20261023-021136)
# differ only on `talk` with `yes`, `no` and `esc` agreeing.
